summary: 100-foot treated timber lookout in the Malheur NF, Grant County, built 1936-37 per most sources; last staffed 2008, condemned after a 2019 inspection, NHLR-registered 2003.

corrections.why: The tower is 100 feet tall (firelookout.com: the present 100' treated timber tower). 2.1 m is not a plausible tower height and looks like a data-entry error.

corrections.proposed: 1936 tower (completed 1937 per archive file); 1940 is the NHLR date for the ground house living quarters
corrections.why: Four sources date the tower to 1936, and the NHLR's own description dates the 1940 construction to the station's ground house, not the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill and The Roaming Civic give 1936 for the tower. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a Malheur National Forest archive file that says the tower was completed in 1937, and a January 7, 1937 newspaper item describes it as already built by CCC enrollees. The archive file gives 1938 for the living quarters and garage, while the NHLR gives 1940 for the ground house. The facts keep the tower's build year out, and the story reports the range.
The NHLR gives 6,280 ft (1,914 m). firelookout.com gives 6290 ft and Cheryl Hill's pages give 6,290 ft. The brief's 1914.1 m matches the NHLR figure. Not in facts.

notes_for_editor: Six page reads and one search. The brief's height_m of 2.1 is a clear error (100 ft, about 30.5 m) and is proposed as a correction. The brief's 1940 build date comes from the NHLR's ground house sentence and is contradicted by the tower dates of 1936-37 elsewhere. The Roaming Civic history also says a 4-year-old boy fell from a landing and died, attributed to the Fire Lookouts of the Northwest book; it gives no date and no second source, so it is left out of the story. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a Glendale Log item from January 1937 and a Burns Times-Herald item from 1943. Story says the 1930s first site was a point about half a mile away; the sources differ on direction (firelookout says southeast, Cheryl Hill says south). Status: NHLR (2019 survey) and Cheryl Hill (2021) describe the tower as condemned and slated for removal; the July 2026 directory calls the site abandoned but legally accessible and warns its information may be out of date. The tower's current condition after 2022 is unverified. The FFLA Facebook post in the search results was not fetched. No photos added; firelookout.com credits photos to the U.S. Forest Service, National Archives and Records Administration, and Rex Kamstra, but no image URLs were extracted.
